france24fr.description: Les Bleus, finalistes de la dernière Coupe du Monde, ont idéalement lancé leur quête d'une troisième étoile mardi en battant le Sénégal (3-1). Les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 étaient à la sortie du match, au MetLife Stadium, pour prendre les réactions des supporters des deux pays.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : Messi et l'Argentine tout simplement trop forts pour l'Algérie
Coupe du monde : l'Argentine et Messi tout simplement trop forts pour l'Algérie
france24fr.description: L'Argentine a nettement dominé l'Algérie (3-0) lors de son premier match dans la compétition. Pour inaugurer son sixième Mondial, Lionel Messi a marqué un triplé, égalant le record de Miroslav Klose de nombre de buts inscrits en Coupe du monde.

france24fr.title: "Rien n'est encore joué" : les Sénégalais gardent espoir malgré la défaite face aux Bleus
france24fr.description: Après leur défaite contre la France pour leur entrée en lice au Mondial 2026, mardi, les Sénégalais ont mis en avant leur bon début de match "contre une très belle équipe". Les Lions de la Teranga se projettent désormais vers la prochaine rencontre, contre la Norvège le 22 juin. France 24 a recueilli leurs impressions.

france24fr.title: En direct : deux pétroliers iraniens ont franchi la zone du blocus américain
france24fr.description: Des pétroliers iraniens ont franchi la zone du blocus américain des ports iraniens qui était en place depuis environ deux mois, a indiqué mercredi le suite de suivi maritime TankerTrackers, avant la signature d'un accord entre Téhéran et Washington prévue vendredi. Le président français Emmanuel Macron a déclaré dans une vidéo diffusée sur le réseau social X que cet accord était "une bonne chose". Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Kylian Mbappé devient le meilleur buteur de l’histoire des Bleus
france24fr.description: Kylian Mbappé ​a battu mardi le record de buts inscrits en ​équipe de France d'Olivier Giroud grâce à ses 57e et 58e réalisations contre le Sénégal, lors du ‌premier match des Bleus à ⁠la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Norvège fait parler sa puissance face à l'Irak et double la France
france24fr.description: La Norvège, victorieuse de l'Irak (4-1) passe devant la France au classement du groupe I après la victoire des Bleus sur le Sénégal un peu plus tôt (3-1). Les Vikings d'Erling Haaland ont fait parler leur puissance face à des Irakiens très joueurs.

france24fr.title: Argentine - Algérie : Lionel Messi en mode triplé pour porter l'Albiceleste
france24fr.description: L'Argentine entre en lice. Pour entamer la défense de son titre de champion du monde, l'Albiceleste de Lionel Messi a dominé l'Algérie de Luca Zidane dans le groupe J du Mondial 2026. Revivez le choc à travers le direct commenté animé par nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Eduardo, un des fils Bolsonaro, écope de quatre ans de prison pour lobbying pour son père
france24fr.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro a été condamné à quatre ans de prison mardi au Brésil pour son lobbying auprès des autorités américaines afin qu'elles intercèdent auprès de son père, l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro, lui-même condamné pour tentative de coup d'État. Il était notamment accusé d'avoir poussé les États-Unis de Donald Trump à des sanctions économiques contre le Brésil.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les supporters français célèbrent la victoire des Bleus face au Sénégal
france24fr.description: La France l'a emporté 3-1 face au Sénégal ce mardi lors de son premier match de poule. À Paris, les supporters sont ravis et rêvent déjà à la suite de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : au Sénégal, des supporters déçus mais confiants pour la suite
france24fr.description: Battu 3-1 par la France malgré une première période encourageante, le Sénégal a manqué de réalisme dans les moments clés. À Dakar, les supporters des Lions réagissent entre déception et espoir pour la suite de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : Mbappé dépasse Giroud, quels records sont les suivants ?
france24fr.description: Face au Sénégal, Kylian Mbappé a marqué mardi son 58e but en équipe de France, dépassant Olivier Giroud en tant que meilleur buteur de l'histoire des Bleus. Et le capitaine tricolore pourrait ne pas s'arrêter là. Tour d'horizon des records qu'il pourrait égaler ou dépasser lors de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Foot : Mbappé continue d'écrire l'Histoire des Bleus
france24fr.description: Depuis la première édition de la Coupe du monde en 1930, l'équipe de France occupe une place à part dans l'histoire du football mondial. En effet, les Tricolores sont l’une des rares nations à avoir participé à la toute première compétition internationale de football, organisée en Uruguay. Pour autant, la France n'était pas encore une nation de football.

france24fr.title: La Réunion : le Parlement adopte une loi de réparation pour les "enfants de la Creuse"
france24fr.description: Le Parlement français a adopté définitivement, mardi, une loi de réparation pour les "enfants de la Creuse", ces plus de 2 000 mineurs réunionnais arrachés à leurs terres et déplacés dans l'Hexagone entre 1962 et 1984. Le texte prévoit la création d'une commission pour la mémoire, l'institution d'une journée nationale d'hommage le 18 février et l'ouverture d'un droit à réparation sous forme d'allocation forfaitaire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Ghanéen Thomas Partey, accusé de viol, ne jouera pas au Canada
france24fr.description: La justice canadienne a rejeté mardi le recours du gouvernement ghanéen qui tentait d'obtenir un visa pour le milieu de terrain Thomas Partey. Accusé de sept viols et d'une agression sexuelle au Royaume-Uni, le joueur s'est vu refuser l'entrée sur le territoire canadien, où le Ghana jouera mercredi son premier match du Mondial 2026 face au Panama.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : effusion de joie à Paris après la victoire des Bleus face au Sénégal
france24fr.description: Longtemps poussive et peu inspirée, la France a finalement réussi ses débuts en Coupe du monde en battant le Sénégal 3-1 grâce notamment à un doublé de Kylian Mbappé, nouveau recordman de buts en bleu. Les supporters qui assistaient au match depuis la fan zone de Paris ont célébré la victoire.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Wenn es um Bürokratie geht, ist die EU unverbesserlich
nzz.description: In der Theorie sind sich fast alle einig: Es gibt zu viele Gesetze. Obwohl von der EU versprochen, gibt es bei der Bürokratisierung keine Trendwende. Dafür brauchte es in Brüssel einen fundamentalen Mentalitätswandel.

nzz.title: Justiz als politische Waffe: Kalifornischer Gouverneur Gavin Newsom wirft Trump Hexenjagd vor
nzz.description: Die Ermittlungen gegen den Demokraten Gavin Newsom sind nur das jüngste Beispiel von Rechtsverfahren, die Donald Trump gegen politische Gegner losgetreten hat. Politisch könnte Newsom vom Kampf mit Trump sogar profitieren.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ GEOPOLITIK» - Das Aus des deutsch-französischen Kampfjets: Was heisst das für Europas Sicherheit?
nzz.description: Es sollte Europas Antwort in einer zunehmend unsicheren Welt werden: ein deutsch-französischer Super-Kampfjet. Doch nach neun Jahren ist das grösste europäische Rüstungsprojekt der Geschichte geplatzt. «Ein fatales Signal», sagt der NZZ- Sicherheitsexperte Georg Häsler.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - 13 Tage über dem Abgrund: Wie eine Frauenseilschaft einen legendären Berg bezwang
nzz.description: Der Schweizer Bergführerin Caroline North und ihrer reinen Frauenseilschaft gelingt ein Coup: Sie klettern die schwierige «South African Route» am Cerro Torre in Patagonien. Dabei machten sie einiges anders als Männer.

nzz.title: Trumps Abkommen mit Iran: In Israel ist nicht nur Netanyahu enttäuscht
nzz.description: Benjamin Netanyahu wollte mit einem Sieg gegen Iran in die Wahlen ziehen. Stattdessen steht der israelische Ministerpräsident vor einem Scherbenhaufen: Politische Gegner und Mitstreiter sehen in dem Abkommen zwischen Iran und den USA eine Niederlage für Israel.

nzz.title: Trumps Jagd nach Irans «Atomstaub» endet ohne eindeutigen Gewinner
nzz.description: In den wochenlangen Verhandlungen zur Beendigung des Krieges haben es die USA nicht geschafft, Iran zur Aufgabe seines Nuklearprogramms zu zwingen. Trotzdem ist die iranische Atomgefahr heute viel geringer als noch vor einem Jahr.

nzz.title: Thomas Tuchel soll England endlich wieder zum WM-Titel führen. Dass er statt auf Starspieler auf Teamgeist setzt, irritiert die Fussballnation
nzz.description: Tuchel bestreitet das erste Turnier als Nationaltrainer – vieles macht der Deutsche anders als seine Vorgänger. Am Mittwoch trifft seine Mannschaft auf Kroatien.

nzz.title: Die reichsten Menschen der Welt: Mansa Musa verschenkte so viel Gold, dass er eine Währungskrise auslöste, Jakob Fugger bestimmte, wer Kaiser wird, und Elon Musk baut eine Stadt auf dem Mond
nzz.description: Elon Musk ist der erste Billionär der Geschichte. Aber ist er auch der reichste Mensch aller Zeiten? Das kommt darauf an, wie man rechnet.

nzz.title: Fünf Tage, fünf Rundkurse: Die Tour de Suisse verliert den Charakter als Landesrundfahrt
nzz.description: Die bewegte Geschichte der Tour de Suisse erhält ein neues Kapitel: Ab Mittwoch fahren Männer und Frauen täglich dieselben Strecken. Der Bedeutungsverlust des einst viertwichtigsten Etappenrennens beschleunigt sich.

nzz.title: Dank China und den USA ist die ganz grosse Energiekrise ausgeblieben. Doch für Entwarnung ist es noch zu früh
nzz.description: China und die USA haben den Erdölmarkt während der Blockade der Strasse von Hormuz stabilisiert. Über dem Schiffsverkehr durch die Meerenge schwebt weiter ein Fragezeichen.

nzz.title: Die E-ID ist ein Prestigeprojekt des Bundes. Jetzt drohen neue Verzögerungen wegen eines Datenschutzproblems
nzz.description: Ursprünglich wollte der Bund die digitale Identitätskarte diesen Herbst einführen. Jetzt wird es wohl 2027. Grund ist unter anderem ein gravierendes Datenschutzproblem mit der AHV-Nummer.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Chefs, die sich für schlauer halten als alle anderen, ist psychologische Sicherheit egal», sagt die Harvard-Professorin Amy Edmondson
nzz.description: Können Mitarbeitende offen ihre Meinung sagen, macht das Teams erfolgreicher: Was sich banal anhört, ist nicht selbstverständlich, sagt die Erfolgsautorin – und wehrt sich gegen den Vorwurf, eine Wohlfühloase im Büro zu propagieren.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - AT1-Anleihen könnten für Banken nützlicher werden
nzz.description: Heute sind die meisten AT1 erst im letzten Moment nutzbar, wenn eine Bank bereits stark unter Druck ist. Ursprünglich war das Instrument eine belastbare Kapitalreserve, die einer Bank zur Verfügung steht, wenn sie noch relativ einfach stabilisiert werden kann.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - «Society 5.0» – was die Schweiz von Japans Weg ohne Zuwanderung lernen kann
nzz.description: Was passiert mit einer Gesellschaft, wenn immer weniger Erwerbstätige immer mehr ältere Menschen finanzieren müssen? Europa beantwortet diese Frage bis jetzt primär mit mehr Zuwanderung. Japan hingegen versucht den demografischen Wandel technologisch zu kompensieren.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Leitungswasser erfüllt hohe Standards. Zwei einfache Massnahmen erhöhen die Qualität noch
nzz.description: Zwei Fachleute halten Wasserfilter für überflüssig und haben bessere Tipps für alle, die Wasser aus dem Hahn trinken.

observador.description: A dias de completar 39 anos, Lionel Messi assinou um hat-trick e igualou Miroslav Klose como melhor marcador da história dos Mundiais. Em campo, chorou — mas disse não estar relacionado com futebol.

observador.title: Comer e ir a banhos: afinal podemos ou não podemos?
observador.description: Todos os verões se repete a mesma regra: esperar depois de comer. Mas será que há mesmo base científica para impedir um mergulho imediato?

observador.description: O antigo primeiro-ministro espanhol está indiciado por tráfico de influências e branqueamento de capitais. Ainda, Reserva Federal norte-americana anuncia hoje a decisão sobre as taxas de juro.

observador.title: O perigo escondido no primeiro jogo de Portugal
observador.description: Portugal estreia-se hoje no Mundial frente ao Congo. O jornalista Miguel Cordeiro analisa o ambiente em Palm Beach e os perigos de um adversário mais incómodo do que parece.

observador.title: 4h. Encontrado corpo de jovem junto à barra de Albufeira
observador.description: Tudo indica que corpo deverá ser do jovem britânico de 23 anos que desapareceu na quinta-feira. Ainda, Roberto Martinez realça que Portugal está unido numa só voz antes da estreia no Mundial.

observador.title: Quatro anos depois, o mundo continua a ser apenas e só dele
observador.description: 200 internacionalizações, primeiro a jogar em seis Mundiais, 16 golos como Klose e o 3.º mais velho a marcar: Messi fez um hat-trick, Argentina bateu Argélia e o mundo não mudou em quatro anos (3-0).

observador.title: 3h. Roberto Martinez: seleção portuguesa fala a uma só voz
observador.description: Na antevisão ao jogo frente à República Democrática do Congo, o selecionador nacional deixou elogios ao adversário. Ainda, foi encontrado um corpo de um jovem junto à barra de Albufeira, em Faro.

observador.title: Atuar como tropa de elite
observador.description: Podemos treinar células para serem comandos no sangue? O imunologista Bruno Silva Santos do GIMM e o ator Tiago Castro debatem uma estratégia para detetar o inimigo camuflado e vencer o cancro.

observador.title: 2h. Mundial 2026. Para Bruno Fernandes não é proibido sonhar
observador.description: Antevisão do jogo de estreia de Portugal no Mundial. Roberto Martinez avança que Ruben Dias não está disponível. Ainda, Irão promete responder de forma "severa" a ataques israelitas no sul do Líbano.

observador.title: É possível fazer qualquer iguaria se a base for Haaland
observador.description: Na partida de estreia na fase final do Mundial, a Noruega venceu o Iraque com dois golos de Haaland, um de Ostigard e outro de Thorstvedt. Pelos iraquianos marcou Ayman Hussein.

observador.title: Pode ignorar-se o sinal da pertença ?
observador.description: O actual Presidente nunca desistirá de atender, proteger, privilegiar os seus - mesmo que aqui e ali os atice ou desespere, nunca esquecerá porém o seu mandamento primeiro: ser amado por todos.

observador.title: Empresas, empresas e empresas
observador.description: Olhando de longe, parece-me que o ministro da Economia não está suficientemente focado nas empresas. Entendo perfeitamente que se preocupe com os fundos europeus e com o PRR. Mas o PRR é passageiro.

observador.title: O português que ganhou bilhete para o Mundial graças à voz
observador.description: A Seleção chegou a hotel InterContinental de Houston sob o apoio de centenas de adeptos. Francisco Vilarinho gritou o nome de todos os jogadores e ganhou um bilhete para o jogo de Portugal.

observador.title: Os reaccionários chocam contra a realidade
observador.description: A globalização e o comércio livre são, sem uma única excepção que valha a pena, o melhor motor de crescimento que a humanidade conhece, e o proteccionismo a forma mais fiável de o desligar.

observador.title: Zeros à esquerda fulos com zeros à direita do Elon
observador.description: Se Musk fosse decente, vendia tudo e dividia a fortuna pelo mundo. Causaria o colapso económico global, sim, mas não seriam 150€ a impedir uma criança em África de ir ao próximo concerto do Bad Bunny.

observador.title: 00h. Irão promete responder a ataques no Líbano
observador.description: Irão diz que vai responder de forma "severa" aos ataques israelitas no sul do Líbano. Ainda, Portugal já chegou a Houston para a estreia no Mundial.

Existing methods assess reliability primarily through output dispersion -- measuring how much sampled answers differ -- but this discards a complementary signal: whether the model can consistently rank competing reasoning candidates.

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a major way for consumers to find products, but we do not yet understand how brands compete in this new channel. We study brand dynamics in LLM recommendations using skincare products -- a category where consumers cannot easily judge quality before buying and must rely on brand reputation -- across three commercial LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 3 Flash), with a robustness check on search goods.

phys-org.title: Frozen Greenland middens preserve 4,500 years of farms, seal hunts and toilets
phys-org.description: Greenland has a long and checkered history of human settlement: several Paleo-Inuit cultures since approximately 2,500 BCE, descendants of Vikings between the 10th and 15th centuries, and early modern Danes since 1721. All left their traces on the landscape, for example in the form of ancient domestic rubbish heaps. Composed of waste like animal bones, excrement, mollusk shells and human artifacts, these middens are a precious resource for archaeologists.

phys-org.title: Heading for the Atlantic Ocean to study the impact of climate change on ocean circulation
phys-org.description: It is becoming increasingly urgent to study the effects of climate change on the global ocean system. Future projections indicate significant changes in the Mediterranean and Atlantic circulation systems, which could have unpredictable climatic consequences, especially for one of the most influential ocean currents in the global climate: the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC).

phys-org.title: Even morphologically similar pollinators carry distinct pollen assemblages
phys-org.description: The body size, morphology and associated behavioral traits of flower-visiting insects strongly influence the quantity of pollen they transport. Thus, pollinators with similar appearances are often assumed to exert similar ecological effects on plants. However, pollinators' effects on plants are not determined solely by the amount of pollen they carry.

phys-org.title: Indian millets contain distinct lipid fingerprints with anti-diabetic and anti-inflammatory potential
phys-org.description: Indian millets are a staple for the country's population of more than a billion. They are also gaining global popularity, with rising exports and a reputation as a climate-resilient crop. Now, new research shows that their nutritional value includes a rich diversity of lipids, including a previously undetected group that may offer potential health benefits. The research is published in the journal Food Chemistry.

phys-org.title: Climate models are missing the first warning signs of deadly Middle East heat waves, study finds
phys-org.description: While the world's most advanced climate models successfully reproduce heat waves once they are underway, they consistently miss key atmospheric processes that trigger these events, potentially limiting the ability to anticipate extreme heat several days in advance.

phys-org.title: Are alien probes hiding in our backyard? A new study says we've barely looked
phys-org.description: Even at this early stage in our spacefaring age, humanity has already begun sending probes that will eventually reach other solar systems, even if that was not their original intention. Five robotic explorers—Pioneer 10 and 11, Voyager 1 and 2, and New Horizons—are all on escape trajectories out of the solar system and might someday enter another one. They will no longer be operational at that point, but they serve as proof of concept that spacefaring civilizations do indeed build interstellar p

phys-org.title: Switzerland map reveals ground light and shade in 10-meter detail
phys-org.description: Researchers have calculated light levels at the ground surface across Switzerland to within 10 meters, in both open and forested areas. The model even simulates the shadows cast by individual trees.

phys-org.title: Dark biodiversity helps solve Darwin's 160-year-old puzzle
phys-org.description: An international research team, which included University of Tartu visiting doctoral student Wen-Gang Zhang and Professor of Botany Meelis Pärtel, has found a new solution to one of ecology's long-standing controversies—Darwin's naturalization conundrum, which addresses the question of why some species successfully establish in a new habitat while others do not. The research is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Ultrasound unlocks protein from cauliflower waste and could add value to existing crops
phys-org.description: An RMIT University innovation uses ultrasound to extract leaf protein from discarded cauliflower leaves, identifying a potential new use for vegetable scraps. The process could help food manufacturers turn vegetable waste into protein ingredients, reducing waste and adding value to existing crops.

phys-org.title: Rethinking plant photoprotection: New insights into antenna protein CP26
phys-org.description: Plants must carefully strike a balance between harvesting sunlight to fuel photosynthesis and protecting themselves from light damage. Part of this balancing act is performed by antenna proteins that are bound to light-harvesting molecules inside plant chloroplasts. Mostly known for harvesting energy from sunlight, some antenna proteins can dissipate excess absorbed energy as heat through a photoprotection mechanism called non-photochemical quenching (NPQ).

phys-org.title: Q&A: Boosting NASA's Swift Observatory to support continued space observation
phys-org.description: NASA's "rapid-response" space telescope is slowly falling out of orbit, but a daring mission this summer could allow the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory to continue scanning the sky for many more years to come. In the first mission of its kind, a spacecraft will launch from Earth and rendezvous with Swift to boost it to a higher altitude and extend its life.

phys-org.title: New method enables accurate sequencing of short peptides hidden in food and human body
phys-org.description: Our food and our bodies are full of tiny protein fragments called peptides. These small chains of amino acids act as biological messengers, influencing processes ranging from sensory perception to physiological functions.

phys-org.title: Vertical marine heat wave study offers classification scheme for coastal resource management
phys-org.description: Marine heat waves (MHWs) are events characterized by prolonged warm coastal and ocean conditions with wide-ranging impacts on ecosystem health and associated industries. While research on MHWs has historically relied on surface-water data from satellite observations and buoy records, new research from the Batten School of Coastal & Marine Sciences & VIMS highlights the need to—quite literally—go deeper.

phys-org.title: AI can clone your voice. Why that's powerful—and dangerous
phys-org.description: Using artificial intelligence, scammers can duplicate someone's voice with just seconds of audio, says the University of Cincinnati's Kimberly Hyun. Impostor scams are one of the most common forms of fraud, according to the Federal Trade Commission.

phys-org.title: Intensive nickel mining has transformed microbial biodiversity of Thio Lagoon in New Caledonia
phys-org.description: A study carried out by scientists from Ifremer, IRD, the universities of Western Brittany (UBO) and Bordeaux, CNRS, and the University of Tartu (Estonia) reveals the impact of nickel mining on the coastal ecosystems of New Caledonia. Published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment, this research shows that starting in the 1950s, the mechanization of mining operations led to a sharp increase in sediment inputs into the Thio Lagoon and a disruption of microbial communities that persist

phys-org.title: Webb and Hubble reveal the history of a relic of Milky Way's formation
phys-org.description: Researchers using two of humanity's most powerful observatories—NASA's James Webb and Hubble Space Telescopes—have definitively shown that Terzan 5 is not a globular star cluster, as it was once classified, offering new insight into how galaxies like our own form and evolve over time.

phys-org.title: Report reveals how digital tools are transforming biodiversity crisis response
phys-org.description: Scientists who study plant physiology and evolution have a new tool in their toolkit: a machine learning algorithm that can scan digital plant specimen collections and quickly measure leaf size and thickness.

phys-org.title: Cotton's roots traced to Yucatan Peninsula, where wild gene pool runs deepest
phys-org.description: There's nothing like this in nature, Jonathan Wendel said as he showed a visitor in his Bessey Hall office the long white puffs billowing from a cotton boll—the protective flower capsule of the plant cultivated by humans for thousands of years. In the wild, cotton bolls are far smaller and hold darker, coarser and shorter fibers.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.

proj-syn.title: Canada’s Great Recalibration
proj-syn.description: The growing fusion of economics, security, and technology has altered the nature of 21st-century interdependence, and Canada has responded by being more intentional. Rather than automatically serving as an extension of US-centered systems, it is creating more options across a wider network of relationships.

proj-syn.title: From Jefferson to Nehru
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence continues to challenge countries, including the US and India, to measure themselves against the ideals they profess. But in a century marked by rising inequality, an authoritarian resurgence, and the emergence of new forms of domination, measuring up will become only more difficult.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Democratic Decline
proj-syn.description: Notwithstanding recent setbacks for illiberal, populist, and authoritarian leaders in some countries, good-governance groups and experts on democratic decline continue to document a disturbing global trend toward “autocratization.” What remains to be seen is whether enough voters will wake up to the threat.

proj-syn.title: The Standard of Independence
proj-syn.description: Although revolutions would surely have occurred had the United States never broken from Britain in 1776, the Declaration of Independence gave later anticolonial movements inspiration and the language to shape their own aspirations. It offered a universal blueprint, even as the US itself adopted the ethos of empire.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of Independence Turns South
proj-syn.description: Whether they were agreeing or arguing, the new countries that emerged across the Americas after the American Revolution influenced each other. Together, they helped shape the global development of modern democracy and the social and political movements that have shaped it ever since.
